Alexander Graham Bell is widely credited as the inventor of the telephone, having been granted U.S Patent No. 174,465 on March 7, 1876. His successful patent application and public demonstration solidified his recognition in this regard. While Antonio Meucci had earlier developed a voice-communication device (though without the necessary resources for formalization), Elisha Gray filed a caveat which was too late to secure precedence over Bell's subsequent U.S Patent Office filing and patent grant.
